reason: The hypothesis synthesizes three distinct strategies—preheating (from P23 on EB-PBF of IN738), laser-clad Inconel 718 transition layers (from P8 on H13 steel), and yttrium microalloying (from P7/P40 on Hastelloy-X)—into a single repair concept for non-weldable Ni-based superalloys, a combination no passage proposes. It also links these through a mechanism of graded thermal expansion matching and oxygen stabilization that none of the sources states, and targets a material (Inconel 713C) and application (repair under cyclic high-temperature service) not addressed by the cited evidence.
copied_elements: Inconel 713C is non-weldable and prone to hot cracking (P3, P6, P17)
Preheating reduces thermal gradients and cracking (P23)
Laser cladding of Inconel 718 as a transition layer (P8, P11)
Yttrium addition to Ni-based superalloys (P7, P40)
